name: Stack (LIFO)
description: Last-In-First-Out structure. Used for backtracking, DFS, parentheses validation, and expression parsing. In JavaScript, stacks are typically implemented using arrays with push() and pop().

examples.title: Example 1: Valid Parentheses
examples.explanation: Push opening brackets onto the stack. For closing brackets, pop the last opening and check if they match. At the end, stack must be empty for a valid string. Time O(n), Space O(n).

examples.title: Example 2: Basic Stack Implementation
examples.explanation: Standard Stack implementation using JS Array. push() and pop() are O(1) amortized. peek() looks at top without removing. All core operations run in constant time.

name: Queue (FIFO)
description: First-In-First-Out structure. Used for BFS, level-order traversal, and task scheduling. In JavaScript, queues are typically implemented using arrays with push() and shift(), though shift() is O(n).

examples.title: Example 1: Basic Queue Implementation
examples.explanation: Standard Queue implementation. enqueue() adds to end (O(1)), dequeue() removes from front (O(n) due to array shift). For production with large queues, use a linked list or circular buffer to achieve true O(1) dequeue.

examples.title: Example 2: BFS Level Order Traversal
examples.explanation: Uses a queue to process tree nodes level by level. The inner for-loop ensures only nodes from the current level are processed before moving to the next. Time O(n), Space O(n) for the queue.

name: Monotonic Stack
description: A stack that maintains elements in monotonic order (either increasing or decreasing). Used for finding next greater/smaller element, sliding window maximum, and histogram area problems.

examples.title: Example 1: Next Greater Element
examples.explanation: Stack stores indices of elements waiting for their 'next greater'. When current element is greater than stack top, we found the answer for that index. Each element is pushed and popped at most once. Time O(n), Space O(n).

examples.title: Example 2: Valid Parentheses with Stack
examples.explanation: Purely stack-based approach. Opening brackets pushed, closing brackets must match the most recent opening. If stack isn't empty at the end, there are unmatched openings. Time O(n), Space O(n).
